steps.note: The curd grains are heated as far as the cheese needs: not at all, or to a scald of 50–56 °C for Emmental, Gruyère and Parmesan.
Whey is drawn off, typically 30–50 % of the batch volume at a time; for Gouda-type cheeses, wash water replaces part of it.
The curd is left in the moulds for about 60–100 minutes, while it acidifies.
The cheese is pressed in 3 to 10 steps of rising pressure, about 50–450 g/cm² depending on the cheese.
Semi-hard cheese is usually brined and ends with 0.5–2 % salt; larger cheeses stay in longer.
The cheese is ripened for periods from none, for fresh cheese, up to months; Gouda is ripened for 2–12 months at 12–15 °C.

sources.text: The usual steps from rennet curd to cheese and the figures given for them; they differ from cheese to cheese, and the handbook's Gouda is the example for brining and ripening.
